meta.title: Scenario Correctness Audit — Three Answers
meta.description: Receipts + verification honesty for the 4 promoted VFR scenarios, the dispatch-contract explainer and skill gap, and the S6 flight_rules backfill

props.title: Skepticism Answered, Honestly
props.subtitle: What was verified, what was rule-based, and where the receipts live — for the 4 promoted VFR scenarios

props.content: Short version: the receipts are real, machine-verified, and on disk; the CLI gates were all replayed by the controller, not trusted. But the skill's strongest clause — a manual row-by-row read of every ownship turn — was done at spot-check depth, not exhaustively, and 12 FMM golds on straight_in_towered were authored by a rule table, not per-turn reality modeling. That is the honest gap, and there is a concrete audit pass proposed below to close it.

props.label: QUESTION 1
props.title: Did we follow the skill? Where are the receipts?
props.subtitle: The verification chain, layer by layer — what each layer actually proves

props.content: The pipeline shape from `/scenario-enrichment-subagents` was followed: review-first editing, receipts recorded through `grounding_lookup.py receipt record` (never hand-authored), promotion only after validator green, then projection → TTS → Thor transcription → targeted baseline → full baseline → self-parity. Receipts live as sidecars in **both** trees: `data/src/partner_graph/review/<id>.receipts.yaml` and the promoted copies at `data/src/partner_graph/sources/partner/<id>.receipts.yaml` (19–25 KB each, all four present). The workstream file records every controller intervention: `.lev/pm/workstreams/scenario-metadata-flight-rules/state/workstream.yaml`.

props.label: QUESTION 1 — THE HONEST PART
props.title: What was NOT done to the letter
Row-by-row review was spot-check depth
props.content: The skill says: 'Review manually row by row. Do not treat CLI validation, receipts, or subagent claims as a substitute for inspecting every ownship turn and every compound segment.' The controller inspected high-risk rows (compound parents, every FMM command, sampled quotes, all worker-claimed-but-missing fields) — but did not produce the skill's Manual Row Audit table for all 52 ownship rows. The workers produced per-row tables; those are claims, and only a subset was independently re-derived.

props.title: 12 FMM golds were rule-authored, not reality-modeled
props.content: The straight_in_towered worker skipped FMM gold on all 12 ownship turns. The controller authored it programmatically: a decision tree mapping intent category → classification (control_action / reporting_obligation / advisory_ack-with-null-command), params trimmed to contract. That is convention-consistent and contract-legal, but it is not the JP ruling's 4-question reality pass ('what happens in the air, does the FMM need to know, what is the readback, what is the payload') applied per turn. Turns like 'descend at pilot's discretion' → altitude_instruction{} deserve a human-grade look.

Dispatch one read-only reviewer agent per scenario (4 total, faa-grounding-agent type) with the skill's Manual Row Audit table as the required output shape: for each of the 52 ownship rows — spoken text, authority class, intent+slots, readback, FMM decision, FAA proof re-derived from the page (not from the receipt), and a verdict. Reviewers are prompted to REFUTE, not confirm. Any defect becomes a bounded repair in `review/` followed by re-promotion through the same gates. Cost: ~4 subagent runs, zero risk (read-only). This converts 'promoted with receipts and spot checks' into 'promoted with a completed per-row audit' — the standard the skill actually sets.

props.label: QUESTION 2
props.title: The dispatch contract, explained
props.subtitle: Why 5 intents fail at the FMM stage with a pure-YAML fix

props.content:
`data/atc/policy/dispatch/command_parameter_contract.yaml` is the typed authority contract, loaded through `modules/authority/command_parameters.py`. Per intent, it declares which slots are **executable parameters** (real FMM authority the fake FMM can act on) versus **context** (explanatory, must never become authority). Dispatch consults it when converting a parsed command into a typed FMM `CommandProposal`, and the anti-cheat law requires a proposal for every ownship command-authority turn — no proposal means fail-closed with `missing_fmm_proposal`, never a silent skip.

When an intent has **no entry at all**, two things happen. Dispatch cannot build a typed proposal, so every scored row expecting one fails at the `fmm_decision` stage. And the projector's gold validation *skips* that intent ('catalog being backfilled') — so the gap is invisible until baseline runs. The five intents the new scenarios exercise with no entry: `cleared_option`, `cleared_touch_and_go`, `short_approach`, `spacing_instruction`, `go_around` — the DS-FM-001 family. The fix is authoring five contract entries with slot roles decided by the reality ruling (e.g. cleared_option: runway executable; go_around: likely no params, the command IS the payload). No module code changes.

props.title: 🩺 Symptom → cause table
props.content:
**missing_fmm_proposal diagnostic** → intent has no contract entry, or dispatch gate dropped the turn.

**'parameters are not declared as executable or context slots'** → gold or dispatch is carrying a slot the contract doesn't declare (the 15 violations trimmed this session; also the pre-existing 360_for_spacing failure — attributed by stash-isolation to the parallel b-fmm lane's drift, not this lane).

**Row passes parser+readback, fails fmm stage** → contract entry missing (DS-FM-001).

**fmm.command.not_applicable on a command turn** → forbidden by anti-cheat; means an upstream gate is being cheated.

props.label: QUESTION 2 — SKILL GAP
props.title: It is NOT in the ratchet skills. Proposal to fix that.
props.subtitle: grep across all six ratchet skills: zero mentions of command_parameter_contract or 'dispatch contract'. The fix_area table has fmm_payload_authority but routes it vaguely to 'naac, ratchet-audit' with no procedure.

props.title: 1️⃣ Contract playbook under fmm_payload_authority
props.content: Add a reference page to ratchet-burndown (reference/fmm-payload-authority.md) and point the fix_area route at it: what the contract owns, the symptom→cause table, the fix procedure (author intents: entry via the 4-question reality ruling; gates: projection --check, targeted baseline, template-rows), and the boundary law (parser slots ≠ FMM params; context never becomes authority; gold must be contract-legal).

props.title: 2️⃣ Surface-ownership map in ratchet-audit
props.content: One 'areas of concern' section mapping the three estates and their hinges: modules/ (authority loader, dispatch, anti-cheat gates — never hardcode vocab), data/ (contract yaml, policy overlays, templates — typed contracts, projector allowlists), scenarios (gold conventions, receipts, promotion gates). Each hinge gets its failure signature, so triage routes by symptom instead of tribal knowledge.

props.title: 3️⃣ Close the silent-skip loophole
props.content: The projector skipping gold validation for contract-less intents ('catalog being backfilled') is exactly how the 5-intent gap stayed invisible. Once DS-FM-001 lands the five entries, propose flipping the skip to a hard error so a NEW intent without a contract entry turns the projection gate red — same philosophy as the template-rows bucket ('that is the point').

props.label: QUESTION 3
props.title: S6 backfill: flight_type → flight_rules
props.subtitle: The deferred slice — mechanical, scoring-inert, one consequence to plan around

props.content:
Today the 244 partner sources carry a free-text `flight_type` field — roughly 50 distinct spellings ('VFR Pattern Work', 'IFR Training Flight', …). The IFR/VFR analysis you asked for had to classify by text heuristics; that worked (242/244 classifiable) but is not queryable truth.

S6 is the backfill: normalize every source's free text into the new typed `flight_rules` enum (ifr / vfr / svfr / dvfr / mixed) that S1 added to the schemas. The 2 genuinely ambiguous scenarios get the field omitted — absent means unknown, never guessed. After it lands, the VFR/BATC demo scorecard becomes a one-line query, and the field is the future key for phase-gated policy loading (your stated down-the-road use).

It was deferred, not forgotten, for sequencing: it touches all 244 sources at once, and grounded sources are hash-pinned.

props.title: The one consequence
props.content: Adding a field to a grounded source changes its source_hash, so the projector marks all ~25 grounded scenarios stale and their output must regenerate. It is metadata-only: no spoken text changes, so NO transcript refresh (per the transcript-churn rule), and scoring stays inert — the parity gate proved the machinery ignores the new fields. Plan: run it as one atomic tick with projection --check + self-parity as its gates.
